# Proofing and supplier production acceptance — facts

> Source-anchored units about Proofing and supplier production acceptance: 19 across 7 sources. Each line ends in the URL and anchor it came from; `keywords:` names the lexicon terms that matched.

<!-- generated by llms-concept-abstractor v1.4.1 · generated 2026-11-06 · 19 units · 7 sources · rights: quote -->

## Structure and components

- [statement] A physical sample must identify its printing process and included finishing. PrintNinja says its assembled game proof can contain digitally printed components that are not color accurate; Kuo Kau says its uncut digital sample uses actual material but excludes coating, varnish and special finishing. (high confidence) — https://printninja.com/proofing-options/ · keywords: Proofing and supplier production acceptance · also: https://www.kkplayingcard.com/en/page-5998/Sample-Proof-Guide.html
- [statement] Publisher Frank West reports checking imposed PDF samples for alignment and cut lines, then counting cards and checking order, duplicates and the rulebook component list. This is a documented operator checklist, not evidence that a supplier performs these checks for the customer. (low confidence) — https://thecityofkings.com/news/requesting-samples-from-your-manufacturer/ · keywords: Proofing and supplier production acceptance
- [statement] PrintNinja warns that digitally printed components within a physical game proof are not color accurate. Physical delivery alone therefore does not establish an offset-color reference for every component. (low confidence) — https://printninja.com/proofing-options/ · keywords: Proofing and supplier production acceptance

## How it works

- [statement] MakePlayingCards’ returns page requests quality-issue contact within 3 days of arrival; its terms describe a 10-day material-and-workmanship warranty. These statements specify different windows and should be quoted separately when agreeing receipt inspection and remedies. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.makeplayingcards.com/guarantee.aspx · keywords: Proofing and supplier production acceptance · also: https://www.makeplayingcards.com/pay_terms.aspx

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] PrintNinja’s published defect clause treats a defect rate under 2% as a completed order. Above 2%, it may provide a proportional refund or reprint and ship replacements at its cost, with the refund/reprint choice reserved to PrintNinja. It may require defect documentation and requires reporting within 90 days of delivery. The clause does not explicitly resolve the exact 2% boundary. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://printninja.com/about/terms/ · keywords: Proofing and supplier production acceptance

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] PrintNinja cautions that a single domestic digital-offset unit cannot be treated as a one-to-one comparison with its offset product because materials, finishes and binding techniques differ. (low confidence) — https://printninja.com/electronic-proofing-steps/ · keywords: Proofing and supplier production acceptance
- [statement] MakePlayingCards tells customers to verify design and order details before submitting: its automated production policy says cancellations and changes cannot be made after submission. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.makeplayingcards.com/guarantee.aspx · keywords: Proofing and supplier production acceptance
- [statement] MakePlayingCards asks customers to report quality issues within 3 days of arrival. Personalized products qualify for return only for a manufacturing error or product defect. A granted remedy can be replacement, refund or account credit after returned items are inspected; the customer is responsible for returning products unused and undamaged. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.makeplayingcards.com/guarantee.aspx · keywords: Proofing and supplier production acceptance
- [statement] MakePlayingCards says cancellations and changes cannot be made after order submission. Its separate terms require written supplier agreement to modified terms, so a buyer should obtain agreement to project-specific acceptance changes before submitting the order. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://www.makeplayingcards.com/guarantee.aspx · keywords: Proofing and supplier production acceptance · also: https://www.makeplayingcards.com/pay_terms.aspx

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Panda describes separate approval gates: approved digital proofs precede sampling; approval of the pre-production copy and component samples starts mass production; review and approval of the mass-production copy precedes assembly of the remaining games. Its mass-production copy arrives when production is nearly complete, so this is an assembly checkpoint rather than a promise that printing has not begun. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://pandagm.com/our-process/ · keywords: Proofing and supplier production acceptance
- [statement] PrintNinja publishes differently scoped color statements: its general board-game explainer calls CMYK hard proofs accurate, but its component-specific proof specification excludes digital components from color accuracy and its terms disclaim guaranteed matching without ordered spot/Pantone color. Attribute these positions and obtain component-specific acceptance terms rather than treating the general statement as a universal guarantee. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://printninja.com/custom-board-games/board-game-prototyping-and-proofing/ · keywords: Proofing and supplier production acceptance · also: https://printninja.com/proofing-options/, https://printninja.com/about/terms/
- [statement] PrintNinja describes soft proofs as layout references rather than reliable previews of printed color. Its electronic-proofing guide explicitly says the screen proof does not establish final colors. (high confidence) — https://printninja.com/about/terms/ · keywords: Proofing and supplier production acceptance · also: https://printninja.com/electronic-proofing-steps/
- [statement] Kylin recommends recording conditional approval in a numbered, revision-controlled report, with both parties retaining its signed or acknowledged final version. This supplies a concrete written revision record rather than an ambiguous approval email. (low confidence) — https://www.kylinmanufactory.com/news/Designing_A_Board_Game/Board_Game_Preproduction_Sample_Approval_Guide.html · keywords: Proofing and supplier production acceptance

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Electronic proofs serve content and layout review, not physical stock or reliable printed-color acceptance: PrintNinja describes PDF layout/trim/fold review and disclaims accurate color; Kuo Kau explicitly excludes physical materials and actual print-color reference from its artwork e-proof. (high confidence) — https://printninja.com/about/terms/ · keywords: Proofing and supplier production acceptance · also: https://www.kkplayingcard.com/en/page-5998/Sample-Proof-Guide.html
- [statement] Kuo Kau distinguishes an offset pre-production sample made on the intended mass-production press and materials from a mass-production sample randomly selected from the completed run; the former targets the closest color match, while the latter checks actual production. (low confidence) — https://www.kkplayingcard.com/en/page-5998/Sample-Proof-Guide.html · keywords: Proofing and supplier production acceptance
- [statement] Frank West uses blank, cut and packaged white samples to evaluate material, dimensions and box fit separately from printed content. His production sample is a manually assembled copy reviewed before the rest are assembled and packed; he warns that correcting errors then may require paying for reprinting or changes. (low confidence) — https://thecityofkings.com/news/requesting-samples-from-your-manufacturer/ · keywords: Proofing and supplier production acceptance
- [statement] PrintNinja requires a submitted and accepted written change order for changes after quotation acceptance and does not guarantee verbal change requests. Its proof terms also say approval can be a button click, written approval or verbal approval, and later changes may incur fees; therefore a revision request must not be confused with an accepted production change. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-06) — https://printninja.com/about/terms/ · keywords: Proofing and supplier production acceptance
- [statement] A publisher operator account describes a mass-production copy as the final publisher quality check before assembly and reports replacing Nut Hunt dice after reviewing that copy. This is a reported experience, not a measured defect rate. (low confidence) — https://www.reddit.com/r/boardgames/comments/136kvuo · keywords: Proofing and supplier production acceptance
- [statement] PrintNinja excludes typos and other content errors from its guarantee and says its prepress review does not check those issues. The buyer must finish content review before approving production. (low confidence) — https://printninja.com/pledge/ · keywords: Proofing and supplier production acceptance
